title: Sufficient positive maps between von Neumann algebras: Rényi divergences
abstract: We prove recovery theorems for $α$-$z$ Rényi divergences under normal unital positive maps between von Neumann algebras. Previous results in this setting required 2-positivity, while recent finite dimensional work showed that this assumption can be relaxed to mere positivity. Our proof uses sufficiency for JW*-subalgebras and $L^p$-spaces over them to characterize equality in the data processing inequality. As a further application of our methods, we solve a problem discussed by Haagerup and Stormer: Every conditional expectation of a von Neumann algebra onto a JW*-subalgebra factors through a conditional expectation onto the generated von Neumann subalgebra.
summary: This work develops recovery theorems for generalized Rényi divergences in the context of von Neumann algebras. It characterizes when the data processing inequality becomes an equality, linking this condition directly to the concept of a 'sufficient' quantum map. This provides deep mathematical insight into information preservation under general quantum operations.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish recovery theorems for $\alpha$-$z$ Rényi divergences when applied to quantum states undergoing evolution via normal unital positive maps between von Neumann algebras.
main_result: Equality in the data processing inequality for these divergences is shown to be equivalent to the map being 'sufficient' with respect to the pair of states, which characterizes the recovery of information.
method: The proof relies on analyzing the equality case of the data processing inequality using $L^p$-spaces associated with $JW^*$-subalgebras and generalizing techniques from the 2-positive setting to mere positivity.
model_or_system: The mathematical framework involves von Neumann algebras ($M, N$) representing the observable structure, and the physical process is modeled by normal unital positive maps ($T: N \to M$) acting as quantum channels.
key_observables: $\alpha$-$z$ quantum Rényi divergences ($D_{\alpha,z}$), the data processing inequality (DPI), and the concept of map sufficiency.
important_parameters: The divergence parameter $\alpha$ and the auxiliary parameter $z$ are crucial, alongside the structure of the von Neumann algebras.
main_assumptions: The initial theorems assume faithfulness of the involved states, though the work aims to relax this. The analysis heavily utilizes the structure of $JW^*$-subalgebras.
paper_structure: The paper develops from general results on the DPI to specific recovery theorems for Rényi divergences, utilizing the algebraic structure of $JW^*$-subalgebras and $L^p$-spaces to generalize previous findings.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools to quantify how much information about a quantum state is preserved (or recoverable) when the state undergoes a general physical process (the map $T$), which is fundamental to quantum channel characterization.
